case.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?

trace.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
trace.answer:
She can't do it on her own. Under [house: Comps], a manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. A $40 comp is over that limit, so the owner has to approve it. The policy says the owner can be reached by text during service.

Two other limits from the same section apply:
- Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount.
- Total comps in a week should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, you review every comp from that week.

She could comp up to $25 herself and send the rest to you. I haven't proposed or filed anything. If you give me the order, I can propose the comp for approval.

case.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?

trace.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?
trace.answer:
You have 30 days from the order date to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order. A dispute filed after that is rejected automatically. [marketplace: Missing or incorrect items]

You can only dispute if you have a packing photo showing the item in the bag. Photos are taken for every marketplace order over $40. If the order was over $40 and there's no photo, don't dispute. Accept the chargeback and log it as a packing miss. [marketplace: Missing or incorrect items]

There is one exception. If the customer is flagged for three or more refunded marketplace orders in the last 90 days, you dispute every missing-item claim whatever the order value, and the owner is told. [marketplace: Repeat disputes]

If you give me an order, I can check its date against the 30-day window.

case.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?

found: messaging: Who may receive marketing texts

trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. Under [messaging: Quiet hours], no text of any kind may go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. For customers with no known local time, use Central time. 10pm falls inside that window, so a promotional text at that hour isn't allowed. Send it between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time instead.

Other rules apply when you do send it:
- Only customers with verified SMS consent can get marketing texts. Implied consent isn't enough, and anyone who has unsubscribed can't be texted at all. [messaging: Who may receive marketing texts]
- A customer can get at most four marketing texts in a calendar month. [messaging: Frequency]
- Any discount is capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve more. The offer must carry an expiry date no more than 14 days out and say "one per customer". [messaging: Offers in messages]

I can't send or schedule texts myself. I can propose a campaign for you to approve if you'd like one.

trace.question: A Grubhub customer complained the food arrived cold. We marked the order ready 15 minutes before it was actually done. Is that on us?
trace.answer:
Yes, this one is on us.

Under the marketplace policy, cold or late deliveries after courier pickup are normally the platform's cost. Grubhub orders have an exception. If we marked the order ready more than 10 minutes before it actually was, the delay counts as ours and we accept the chargeback. Marking it ready 15 minutes early is over that 10-minute limit. So we shouldn't dispute the chargeback. The same policy says not to refund or credit the customer ourselves for platform delivery problems, but here the chargeback is the way we absorb the cost. I haven't looked up the specific order. If you give me the order number, I can check its details.

trace.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
trace.answer:
Not as written. The system blocked my proposal for a 20% text deal because it's over the 15% cap.

The policy caps text discounts at 15% or $10, whichever is lower. Going higher needs the owner's approval [messaging: Offers in messages]. The check blocked it outright, and nothing has been sent or scheduled.

You could still reach 56 customers. They have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. Customers who only gave a phone number when ordering can't get marketing texts, and neither can anyone who has unsubscribed [messaging: Who may receive marketing texts]. 56 is well under the 500-customer limit [messaging: Audience size].

The offer has to state an expiry date no more than 14 days out and say "one per customer." Texts can't go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time [messaging: Quiet hours].

My draft said "20% off your next order, one per customer, valid through 2026-11-03. Reply STOP to opt out." If you want something that can go ahead, I can re-propose it at 15% or less. For 20%, the owner would have to approve it separately.
